primary_conclusion: Gradient variance reduction concerns estimator precision for the same proxy objective, not objective alignment or classification improvement. CF changes scores but no B argmax prediction at the six fixed S-full endpoints.
scope_limitations: 32 paired G8 MC gradient estimates at final CF models, not exact stochastic expectations.
The new derivative estimate uses PATH for the same differentiable objective at the CF point; it is not a newly trained PATH arm.
Only S-full contexts analyzed; does not identify all transient or half-support trajectories.
Teacher already saw full TRAIN, B is module-training data, not independent validation.
KL opposition or small changes do not prove removing KL or widening actions improves generalization.
Sampling U below deterministic U is descriptive; it does not alone explain failed deployment.
No new VAL/F scoring or parameter/endpoint selection; existing frozen gates and results unchanged.

proposed_next_work.priority_1: Separate action-space anchoring from reward gradient using a prospectively frozen matched diagnostic; keep CE and same action space, replace coordinate-level trust constraint with explicit decision-preservation measurement, not a VAL lambda sweep.
proposed_next_work.priority_2: Use genuine class-correct rescue/harm and deployment-aligned hard decision checks as the endpoint objective for any new RL design; continuous sigmoid utility remains diagnostic rather than being equated with classification success.
proposed_next_work.priority_3: If useful flips cannot be induced in the constrained single-prototype family, test a structurally different evidence-set/multimode action space under fixed capacity. Ordinary multiprototype capacity, supervised selection and exact/enumerated expectation controls remain required.
proposed_next_work.not_admitted: No R99 launch, no guarantee of improvement or novelty; old closed branches and original R98 stop remain respected.
